candidate: 名画一瞥 / Art at a glance

content_screening.scope: Only official records with share_license_status=CC0, type=Painting, a valid official web JPEG, usable dimensions and declared byte size enter the pool. Title plus description are rejected when they contain configured sexual, nudity, graphic violence or self-harm terms.
content_screening.visual_sample: Several separate four-image Chromium rounds were inspected. They contained landscapes, religious scenes, and manuscript-style garden scenes. No explicit sexual act, visible genitalia, or graphic injury was observed; one religious painting prominently showed a bare male torso with a waist cloth and small angelic child figures. This proves that metadata keyword filtering reduces risk but does not exclude nonsexual partial nudity in religious or mythological art.
content_screening.limitations: The API has no machine-readable age rating. A random external visual game cannot guarantee absence of every culturally sensitive motif. Any later report should stop that round rather than silently fetch a replacement.

media_boundary.image_cors: No Access-Control-Allow-Origin header observed; ordinary img embedding works and the game never uses canvas.
media_boundary.browser_enforcement: The component validates the exact HTTPS image host and _web.jpg path, trusts the official API's reported filesize for the 1.2 MB / 4.0 MB selection budget, removes image src at the 10 s timeout, and requires successful browser decode before enabling play. Actual transfer size is determined by the museum response.
media_boundary.clue_reuse: After all four candidate Image elements decode, the answer Image is drawn into a 960x420 clue canvas. The canvas makes no second remote reference, so the protocol uses exactly four media URLs without relying on a cache hit. The cross-origin image taints the canvas by design; the game never reads or exports it.
media_boundary.live_audit_enforcement: The maintenance probe additionally streams each image with AbortController, verifies image/jpeg, and cancels on actual byte-cap or time-cap breach.
media_boundary.hard_limit_caveat: Because the image CDN does not permit CORS reads, production img elements cannot inspect response headers or count actual bytes. The 4.0 MB production cap is therefore a trusted official-metadata cap, not a byte-perfect transport cap. Enforcing a byte-perfect cap would require a CORS-enabled image endpoint or a proxy, both outside this project boundary.
